title: The Lost Puppy
description: Read the story, then answer the questions in your own words.
story:
One afternoon, Sara was walking home from school when she heard a small barking sound behind a tree. She looked and saw a tiny puppy shivering in the cold. The puppy had no collar and looked very hungry.

Sara gently picked up the puppy and took it home. She gave it some food and water. Later that evening, Sara and her father made posters to help find the puppy's owner.

The next day, a neighbor saw the poster and came to Sara's house. The puppy happily ran to the neighbor because it belonged to him. The neighbor thanked Sara for taking care of his puppy.

Sara felt happy because she helped someone in need.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
description: Read this classic fable, then answer the questions.
story:
All summer long, the ant worked hard. Every day she carried food to her nest underground. The grasshopper watched and laughed. Why do you work so hard? he sang. Come play with me instead! The ant shook her head. Winter is coming. I must prepare.

When winter arrived, the grasshopper was cold and hungry. He had nothing stored away. He knocked on the ant's door and begged for food. The ant shared a little, but said kindly, Next summer, remember to work while the sun shines.

The grasshopper nodded and promised he would never forget that lesson again.

acceptableAnswers: shared food and told him to prepare next time

title: What Are Fractions?
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Fractions Are Parts
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CA9XLJpQp3c
(Copy the link into your browser and watch before you start!)

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FRACTION — A fraction shows a part of a whole.
   Imagine a pizza cut into 4 equal slices.
   If you eat 1 slice, you ate 1/4 (one-fourth) of the pizza.
   The pizza = the WHOLE. Your slice = the PART.

NUMERATOR — The TOP number of a fraction.
   It tells HOW MANY equal parts you have.
   In 3/8 → the numerator is 3 (you have 3 parts).

DENOMINATOR — The BOTTOM number of a fraction.
   It tells how many EQUAL PARTS the whole is cut into.
   In 3/8 → the denominator is 8 (the whole is cut into 8 parts).

REMEMBER:
   Denominator = Down (it is the number on the bottom!)
   3/8 means: 3 parts OUT OF 8 equal parts total.

EXAMPLES:
   1/2 = one-half (whole cut into 2, you have 1)
   3/4 = three-fourths (whole cut into 4, you have 3)
   5/6 = five-sixths (whole cut into 6, you have 5)

questions.prompt: In the fraction 3/8, which number is the NUMERATOR?
In the fraction 3/8, which number is the DENOMINATOR?
What does the NUMERATOR tell you?
acceptableAnswers: how many equal parts we have

questions.prompt: What does the DENOMINATOR tell you?
acceptableAnswers: how many equal parts the whole is cut into

A shape is divided into 3 equal parts. You shade 1 part. Write the fraction shaded.

CHALLENGE: If a fraction has the same numerator AND denominator (like 4/4), how much of the whole does it represent?

title: Types of Fractions: Proper, Improper & Mixed Numbers
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Types of Fractions
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=17IgK9b6P2M

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PROPER FRACTION — The numerator is SMALLER than the denominator.
   The fraction is LESS than 1 whole.
   Examples: 1/2  3/4  5/8  2/3
   Think: proper = small top, big bottom.

IMPROPER FRACTION — The numerator is EQUAL TO or LARGER than the denominator.
   The fraction equals OR is MORE than 1 whole.
   Examples: 5/4  7/3  9/9  11/6
   Think: improper = big top (or equal top and bottom).

MIXED NUMBER — A WHOLE NUMBER combined with a proper fraction.
   It shows the same amount as an improper fraction but in a friendlier way.
   Examples: 1 1/2 (one and a half)   2 3/4 (two and three-fourths)

CONVERTING IMPROPER ↔ MIXED:
   IMPROPER → MIXED: Divide numerator by denominator.
      7/3 → 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1 → write as 2 1/3
   MIXED → IMPROPER: Multiply whole × denominator, then add numerator.
      2 1/3 → (2×3)+1 = 7 → write as 7/3

title: Equivalent Fractions
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Equivalent Fractions (search on YouTube or visit mathantics.com)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFPCkFnSqjk

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

EQUIVALENT FRACTIONS — Fractions that look different but have the SAME VALUE.
   1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8   (all equal one-half!)
   Think: same SIZE slice, just cut into more pieces.

HOW TO FIND EQUIVALENT FRACTIONS:
   Multiply OR divide BOTH top and bottom by the SAME number.

   MULTIPLY UP:   1/3 × 2/2 = 2/6    (multiply top AND bottom by 2)
                  1/3 × 3/3 = 3/9    (multiply top AND bottom by 3)

   DIVIDE DOWN:   6/8 ÷ 2/2 = 3/4    (divide top AND bottom by 2)
                  4/6 ÷ 2/2 = 2/3    (divide top AND bottom by 2)

REMEMBER: You must do the SAME thing to both top and bottom!
   This is like multiplying or dividing by 1, so the value never changes.

title: Simplifying Fractions
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Simplifying Fractions
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AtBUQH8Tkqc

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SIMPLEST FORM / SIMPLIFYING — Making a fraction as small and simple as possible.
   A fraction is in SIMPLEST FORM when there is no number (except 1)
   that divides evenly into BOTH the top and bottom.

GREATEST COMMON FACTOR (GCF) — The biggest number that divides evenly
   into BOTH the numerator and denominator.
   This is the number you divide by to simplify.

STEP-BY-STEP:
   1. Find the GCF of the numerator and denominator.
   2. Divide BOTH by the GCF.
   3. The result is the fraction in simplest form.

EXAMPLES:
   Simplify 4/8:
      Factors of 4: 1, 2, 4
      Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8
      GCF = 4  →  4÷4 / 8÷4  =  1/2  ✓

   Simplify 6/9:
      GCF of 6 and 9 = 3  →  6÷3 / 9÷3  =  2/3  ✓

   Simplify 10/15:
      GCF of 10 and 15 = 5  →  10÷5 / 15÷5  =  2/3  ✓

TIP: If both numbers are even, start by dividing by 2.

title: Comparing Fractions
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Comparing Fractions
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KNdUJQ_qd4U

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

COMPARING FRACTIONS — Finding out which fraction is bigger, smaller, or equal.
   Use the symbols:  >  (greater than)  <  (less than)  =  (equal to)

RULE 1 — SAME DENOMINATOR:
   When the denominators are the SAME, just compare the numerators!
   3/8  vs  5/8  →  3 < 5  so  3/8 < 5/8

RULE 2 — SAME NUMERATOR:
   When the numerators are the SAME, the fraction with the SMALLER denominator is BIGGER.
   (Fewer cuts = bigger pieces!)
   1/3  vs  1/5  →  thirds are bigger than fifths  so  1/3 > 1/5

RULE 3 — DIFFERENT TOP AND BOTTOM:
   Find a COMMON DENOMINATOR first, then compare.
   2/3 vs 3/4:
      Common denominator = 12
      2/3 = 8/12   and   3/4 = 9/12
      8/12 < 9/12   so   2/3 < 3/4

BENCHMARK: Compare to 1/2 to get a quick sense.
   Less than 1/2 = small.   More than 1/2 = large.

title: Fractions on a Number Line
description: Read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions. Use the number line in your head or draw one on paper!
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Khan Academy — Fractions on a Number Line
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vmu3X4FVbSY

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

NUMBER LINE — A line with numbers in order, evenly spaced.
   Fractions live BETWEEN 0 and 1 (and beyond 1)!

HOW TO PLACE A FRACTION:
   The denominator tells you HOW MANY equal parts to split the space between whole numbers.
   The numerator tells you HOW MANY of those parts to count.

EXAMPLE: Place 3/4 on a number line:
   The denominator is 4, so split 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts.
   Count 3 parts from 0:  0 --- 1/4 --- 2/4 --- 3/4 --- 4/4(=1)
   3/4 is 3 steps from 0.

EXAMPLE: Place 5/3 on a number line:
   5/3 is an improper fraction (bigger than 1).
   5/3 = 1 whole + 2/3 more → it sits between 1 and 2 on the number line.

FRACTIONS BETWEEN WHOLE NUMBERS:
   All proper fractions (like 1/4, 2/3) are between 0 and 1.
   1 1/2 is between 1 and 2.  2 3/4 is between 2 and 3.

title: Adding Fractions with the Same Denominator
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Adding and Subtracting Fractions
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5juto2ze8Lg

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ADDING FRACTIONS — When adding fractions with the SAME denominator:
   Step 1: Keep the denominator THE SAME.
   Step 2: Add ONLY the numerators.
   Step 3: Simplify if possible.

   THINK: The denominator tells you the size of each piece.
          If pieces are the same size, just count (add) them!

EXAMPLES:
   2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5  (add tops: 2+1=3, keep bottom: 5)
   3/8 + 4/8 = 7/8
   4/6 + 2/6 = 6/6 = 1 (the fraction equals 1 whole!)

IF THE SUM IS IMPROPER, convert to a mixed number:
   5/4 + 3/4 = 8/4 = 2 (divide 8 by 4)
   3/4 + 3/4 = 6/4 = 1 2/4 = 1 1/2

DO NOT add the denominators!
   2/5 + 1/5 ≠ 3/10   (this is WRONG!)
   2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5    (this is CORRECT!)

title: Subtracting Fractions with the Same Denominator
description: Watch the video first (same video as Day 7), then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Adding and Subtracting Fractions
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5juto2ze8Lg
(Rewatch or continue from where you stopped.)

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SUBTRACTING FRACTIONS — When subtracting fractions with the SAME denominator:
   Step 1: Keep the denominator THE SAME.
   Step 2: Subtract ONLY the numerators.
   Step 3: Simplify if possible.

EXAMPLES:
   5/8 - 2/8 = 3/8   (subtract tops: 5-2=3, keep bottom: 8)
   7/9 - 4/9 = 3/9 = 1/3   (then simplify!)
   1 - 3/4 = 4/4 - 3/4 = 1/4   (write 1 as 4/4 first)

SUBTRACTING FROM A WHOLE NUMBER:
   To subtract a fraction from 1, rewrite 1 as n/n first.
   1 - 2/5 = 5/5 - 2/5 = 3/5
   1 - 7/8 = 8/8 - 7/8 = 1/8

description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NybHckSEQBI

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ALGEBRA — A branch of math where we use LETTERS to stand for unknown numbers.
   Think of a letter as a mystery box 📦 hiding a number inside.
   Your job is to figure out what number is in the box!

VARIABLE — A LETTER that stands for an unknown number.
   x, n, a, b, y are all common variables.
   Example: x + 3 = 7  →  x is the unknown number.

EXPRESSION — A math phrase with numbers, variables, and operations.
   It has NO equals sign.
   Examples: 3x     n + 5     8 - y     2a

EQUATION — A math SENTENCE with an equals sign (=).
   It says two things are EQUAL.
   Examples: n + 5 = 12     3x = 18     y - 4 = 6

EVALUATING — Finding the value of an expression when you know the variable.
   If n = 4:   n + 7 = 4 + 7 = 11
   If x = 3:   5x = 5 × 3 = 15

NOTE: In algebra, a number next to a letter means MULTIPLY.
   3x means 3 × x     5n means 5 × n

title: Solving Addition & Subtraction Equations
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Solving Basic Equations Part 1 (Addition & Subtraction)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l3XzepN03KQ

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SOLVING AN EQUATION — Finding the value of the variable that makes the equation TRUE.

THE GOLDEN RULE OF ALGEBRA:
   Whatever you do to ONE side of the equation, you MUST do to the OTHER side too!
   This keeps the equation balanced (like a scale ⚖️).

SOLVING x + a = b:
   SUBTRACT a from BOTH sides to get x alone.
   x + 5 = 12
   x + 5 - 5 = 12 - 5
   x = 7  ✓
   CHECK: 7 + 5 = 12 ✓

SOLVING x - a = b:
   ADD a to BOTH sides to get x alone.
   x - 4 = 9
   x - 4 + 4 = 9 + 4
   x = 13  ✓
   CHECK: 13 - 4 = 9 ✓

ALWAYS CHECK your answer by substituting it back into the original equation!

INVERSE OPERATIONS:
   Addition ↔ Subtraction  (they undo each other)

title: Solving Multiplication & Division Equations
description: Watch the video first, then read the Key Vocabulary and answer the questions.
story:
📺 WATCH FIRST!
Math Antics — Solving Basic Equations Part 2 (Multiplication & Division)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qyd_v3DGzTM

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
KEY VOCABULARY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SOLVING a × n = b  (multiplication equation):
   DIVIDE both sides by a to get n alone.
   4 × n = 28
   4 × n ÷ 4 = 28 ÷ 4
   n = 7  ✓
   CHECK: 4 × 7 = 28 ✓

SOLVING n ÷ a = b  (division equation):
   MULTIPLY both sides by a to get n alone.
   n ÷ 3 = 5
   n ÷ 3 × 3 = 5 × 3
   n = 15  ✓
   CHECK: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 ✓

INVERSE OPERATIONS:
   Multiplication ↔ Division  (they undo each other)

REMEMBER:
   3n means 3 × n
   To undo multiplication, DIVIDE.
   To undo division, MULTIPLY.
   ALWAYS check your answer by substituting back in!

title: Surah An-Nazi'at — Complete (All 46 Ayat)
description: Read ALL 46 ayat with your parent. Read the transliteration and meaning aloud for each ayah. Then answer the questions!
story:
SURAH AN-NAZI'AT (Those Who Pull Out) — Surah 79 — All 46 Ayat

── PART 1: THE POWERFUL ANGELS (Ayat 1-5) ──
1. Wan-nazi'ati gharqa — By those [angels] who extract [souls] forcefully
2. Wan-nashitati nashta — And [by] those who remove [them] gently
3. Was-sabihati sabha — And [by] those who glide [through the heavens]
4. Fas-sabiqati sabqa — And those who race ahead
5. Fal-mudabbirati amra — And those who carry out Allah's command

── PART 2: THE DAY OF JUDGMENT (Ayat 6-14) ──
6. Yawma tarjufur-rajifah — On the Day the earth will tremble with a great shaking
7. Tatba'uhar-radifah — Followed by a second shaking
8. Quloobun yawma-ithin wajifah — Hearts that Day will be trembling
9. Absaruha khashi'ah — Their eyes cast down in humility
10. Yaqooloona a-inna lamar-dooduna fil-hafirah — [The disbelievers say] Will we really be brought back to our former state?
11. A-itha kunna 'izaman-nakhirah — Even after we have become crumbled bones?
12. Qaloo tilka ithan karratun khasirah — They say that would be a losing return!
13. Fa-innama hiya zajratun wahidah — It will be only ONE blast
14. Fa-itha hum bis-sahirah — And suddenly they will be on the open plain

── PART 3: THE STORY OF MUSA AND FIRAUN (Ayat 15-26) ──
15. Hal ataka hadeesu musa — Has the story of Musa (Moses) reached you?
16. Ith nadahu rabbuhoo bil-wadil-muqaddasi tuwa — When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa
17. Ithhab ila fir'awna innahu tagha — Go to Pharaoh (Firaun) — indeed he has transgressed!
18. Faqul hal laka ila an tazakka — And say to him: Would you like to purify yourself?
19. Wa-ahdiyaka ila rabbika fatakhsha — And I will guide you to your Lord so you may fear Him.
20. Fa-arahu al-ayatal-kubra — So Musa showed Firaun the greatest sign (miracle)
21. Fa-kaththaba wa 'asa — But Firaun denied it and disobeyed
22. Thumma adbara yas'a — Then he turned away, striving [against Allah]
23. Fahashara fanaada — He gathered his people and announced
24. Faqala ana rabbukumul-a'la — I am your most exalted lord!
25. Fa-akhadhahul-lahu nakalal-akhirati wal-oola — So Allah punished him severely as a warning for the last and the first
26. Inna fee thalika la-'ibratan liman yakhsha — Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears Allah

── PART 4: ALLAH'S CREATION (Ayat 27-33) ──
27. A-antum ashaddu khalqan amis-sama? Banaha — Are you harder to create, or is the heaven? Allah constructed it!
28. Rafa'a samkaha fasawwaha — He raised its height and proportioned it perfectly
29. Wa-aghtasha laylaha wa-akhraja duhaha — He darkened its night and brought out its light
30. Wal-arda ba'da thalika dahaha — And after that He spread out the earth
31. Akhraja minha ma'aha wa-mar'aha — He brought out from it its water and its pastures
32. Wal-jibala arsaha — And the mountains He set firmly in place
33. Mata'al-lakum wa-li-an'amikum — As provision for you and your animals

── PART 5: THE FINAL JUDGMENT (Ayat 34-41) ──
34. Fa-itha ja'atit-tammatul-kubra — But when the greatest catastrophe comes
35. Yawma yatathakkarul-insanu ma sa'a — The Day when man will remember everything he did
36. Wa-burrizatil-jaheemu liman yara — And Hellfire will be shown to all who can see
37. Fa-amma man tagha — As for he who transgressed
38. Wa-athara al-hayatad-dunya — And preferred the life of this world
39. Fa-innal-jaheema hiyal-ma'wa — Then indeed Hellfire will be his home
40. Wa-amma man khafa maqama rabbihi wa-nahannafsا 'anil-hawa — But as for he who feared standing before his Lord and restrained his desires
41. Fa-innal-jannata hiyal-ma'wa — Then indeed Paradise will be his home

── PART 6: THE HOUR (Ayat 42-46) ──
42. Yas-aloonaka 'anis-sa'ati ayyana mursaha — They ask you: When is the Hour [of Judgment]?
43. Feema anta min thikraha — Who are you to say when it is?
44. Ila rabbika muntahaha — Its knowledge rests only with your Lord
45. Innama anta munthiru man yakhshaha — You are only a warner for those who fear it
46. Ka-annahum yawma yarawna ha lam yalbathu illa 'ashiyyatan aw duha — On the Day they see it, it will feel as if they only stayed [in this world] for an afternoon or a morning
